co_west_slabs.blurb: A south-facing crag on the hillside above the old mine workings at Silver Plume, roughly 200 feet over the tailings. Eleven routes, mostly traditional with a couple of bolted lines, and a mix of fully bolted, gear-only and hybrid protection. Grades run from 5.5 up to the low 5.12s, with a bunch of 5.7s and 5.9s in the middle and two hard 5.12 lines drawing the attention. Most climbs are a single pitch of 60 to 150 feet, so one 60 m rope is usually enough, and one three-pitch route reaches about 300 feet. The wall is steeper and tougher than the long slabs on nearby Monument Rock. It catches strong sun, and the elevation keeps the comfortable season to the warm months. Not every route has bolted anchors.

co_zone_1.blurb: The first cluster of routes met when heading up Unaweep Canyon past Don Juan, near Grand Junction. The climbs sit on and above a slabby apron of granite, separated from the next zone by a loose, low-angle bulge. Eleven routes, nearly all listed as trad, with single-pitch lines of about 70 to 100 feet plus a few multi-pitch climbs. Many of the shorter routes are bolted with optional gear. The grades lean hard: mostly 5.10s and 5.11s, with a couple of easier lines around 5.8 and 5.9. Rock is generally good, but anchors on some routes are poor and a few lines wander to nowhere, so bring your own gear and judgment. Expect desert cactus on the walk in.

co_sex_cave.blurb: A steep, roofed cave on the north side of Clear Creek Canyon near Golden, also known as Pete's Wicked Cave. Nearly everything here is sport, with a single boulder problem across the creek. The routes are short, roughly 30 to 50 feet, with tricky cruxes and demanding finger strength, and the grades sit almost entirely in the 5.12s to 5.13s, so it is a place for strong climbers. Most draws are fixed. Because it faces north it stays shaded and cold in winter but offers relief on hot days, which makes it a good summer crag; spring and fall also work. The walk from the road is under five minutes.
